top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only awardable proposal on the slate, and I rank him first on literary merit, not on the unanimity of the earlier rounds. On public knowledge of the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid, his voice is distinctive. He joins memory, the body, dream and cosmological speculation in dense, recursive, image-driven prose, sustained at large scale over decades, with a lyric root in his poetry. The attribution is clean: one writer, one language. The citation is best weighted toward the major prose, with the poetry named as its lyric origin, because translated coverage of the poetry and early work is uneven. Three uncertainties remain open. First, how much of the Romanian rhythm, wordplay and syntax survives in translation; I have not read the originals or independently verified any text. Second, whether Solenoid widens the project begun in Blinding or restages it, which I lean toward the former but have not tested against the books. Third, whether a Romanian-language expert assessment would confirm the case. Even so, none of the alternatives, which the discussion treated as fallbacks (Carson, Can Xue, Michon), has a clearly stronger case on voice, form and sustained depth. P000 is ranked last because I judge the case for an award to be adequate on the evidence available.
recusal_note: none apparent from the supplied profile. I have no documented personal or professional tie to Cărtărescu. I have said publicly that the Academy has overlooked many significant women's authorships; that is a general statement about the Academy's record, not a reason to favor or disfavor any candidate, and I have kept it out of my merit assessment.
